title: A wallet on the N train seat. C$300 inside, and an ID from Ditmars.

options.label: Return it all
options.get: A clean conscience, maybe a thank-you

outcomes.text: You hand it to Yesenia at the booth. She writes your name down like it matters. It does.

later.text: Remember the wallet on the N? Its owner tracked you down at Sal's with a thank-you card and a C$60 bodega credit.

options.label: Keep the cash, return the wallet
options.riskWhy: The owner knows what was in it

outcomes.text: You drop the empty wallet at the booth. C$300 richer and slightly unable to make eye contact with yourself.
C$300 in your pocket, wallet at the booth. Clean getaway, for now.

later.text: The wallet's owner posted a station camera still of whoever returned it 'a little lighter'. People in Astoria have eyes.

options.label: Keep it all
options.riskWhy: The ID has a face. So do you.

outcomes.text: Wallet in your pocket. It's a nice wallet, which somehow makes it worse.

later.text: Remember the wallet on the N? Its owner posted a 'have you seen this person' flyer. It looks a lot like you.

title: Your Hailr ride from Flushing glitched: C$0 for a C$48 trip. Driver Ramón doesn't know yet.

options.label: Report it and pay
options.get: Ramón gets paid, and a five-star from him

outcomes.text: You flag the glitch. The app sends a C$48 bill and a survey about how the glitch made you feel. Ramón honks twice, happily.
Free ride across Queens. You tip Ramón zero stars of guilt and get out at Ditmars humming.
Free ride. Ramón asks if the app is working. You say 'seems fine.' Technically it is, for you.

later.text: Remember the C$0 Hailr ride from Flushing? The app found it. C$48, a C$15 'glitch recovery fee' and a rider rating of 3.9.

outcomes.text: You pay the C$48 and add twelve. Ramón says you're the first passenger in a month who didn't eat in his car.

later.text: Remember paying Ramón for the glitched Flushing ride? He picked you up again and waved off the fare: 'You're the honest one.'

title: Showtime on the 7! You caught the backflip on camera. It's better than anything you've ever posted.

options.label: Post it and tag the dancers
options.get: Some clout, and the crew's thanks
options.cost: Half the views go to them
options.riskWhy: Credit is hard to get wrong

outcomes.text: You post it with the crew's handle. They repost it with three fire emojis. That's a handshake on the 7.

later.text: Remember tagging the showtime crew on the 7? They shouted you out in their next video: 'the only camera that asked.'

outcomes.text: The clip takes off. People in the comments ask where to find 'your' dancers. You reply with a mysterious emoji.
The clip takes off overnight. Someone asks who the dancers are. You let the question sit.

later.text: Remember posting the showtime clip with no credit? The crew from the 7 found it. Their stitch, 'who is this?', has twice your views.

options.label: Tip C$10 and ask first
options.get: Their blessing and a better angle
options.cost: C$10, and you miss your stop

outcomes.text: You tip and ask. They do the flip again, for you, at 61st Street. You end up in Woodside, but the clip is perfect.

title: On the N, Chardonnay Shade's assistant is on speaker: the 'surprise' engagement is a spin-off promo.

outcomes.text: You put your headphones in like a civilized New Yorker. The assistant keeps talking. You keep not listening, mostly.
Lola pays C$150 and runs it as BREAKING within the hour. 'Sources on the N tell me...' You are the source on the N.

later.text: Remember the call on the N? Chardonnay's assistant got fired, and the follow-up names 'a source in a green jacket.' Everyone knows your jacket.

outcomes.text: 'Some engagements are just marketing 👀.' Two hundred people ask what you mean. You say nothing. Power.
Your teaser gets decoded by a fan account in nine minutes. Clout now, and a fan army in your mentions.
